title: ICE hypercomplex hypothesis-testbench research graph
description: A repository-local memory and index graph for the finite Cayley-Dickson and sedenion calculations. It separates computed algebraic facts, interpretation, invalid or superseded methods, and open physical hypotheses without promoting the corpus to a Standard Model embedding or TOE.

quick_answers.question: What does the robust number 42 count?
quick_answers.answer: The direct calculation distinguishes 42 unordered assessor axis-planes (seven classes of six), 84 signed vectors e_a +/- e_b with a<b, and 168 representations when both index orders are counted. Annihilating-pair totals need their own sign and ordering convention; none of these counts establishes 42 Higgs particles.

quick_answers.question: Did the projected custodial SU(2) x SU(2) construction close?
quick_answers.answer: No. All 42 frozen candidates fail both projected closure conditions; the later portability audit also finds combined rank three rather than the required rank six.

quick_answers.question: Can Queue 03 be used as portable threshold evidence?
quick_answers.answer: No. Its entrywise commutator maximum changes under an orthogonal change of null-space basis, so its threshold categories are quarantined as NONPORTABLE_FAIL and provide no new physics verdict.

quick_answers.question: Was a g2 representation established by the projected sedenion construction?
quick_answers.answer: No. The original projection is a method artifact. A later sidecar recovers rank 14 and antisymmetry, but its declared full Lie-closure and Casimir validation is contradicted by the recorded controls.

quick_answers.question: Was an explicit S3 automorphism subgroup computed?
quick_answers.answer: Yes within the declared Cayley-Dickson convention: the two generators preserve all tested products, satisfy the S3 presentation, and generate a group of order six. A later finite action audit finds that the two generators centralize the computed 14-dimensional derivation space, and a separate two-convention audit finds that they preserve the transcribed Wilmot eq-9 theta tensor. These results do not prove the full global automorphism-group decomposition. The older claim that this refuted Wilmot was withdrawn.

quick_answers.question: Did the sealed Claim B calculations support a stable infinite Cayley-Dickson tower limit?
quick_answers.answer: No under their preregistered finite-level criteria. The n=5..7 nullity distributions remain far apart, the n=4..7 associator distributions reconfigure, and the recorded prediction family fails its declared Cauchy-decreasing predicate. This kills that finite statistical route; it neither constructs nor universally disproves an infinite-dimensional path integral or a gravity map.

nodes.title: Hypercomplex hypothesis testbench
nodes.summary: Finite Cayley-Dickson and sedenion calculations plus explicit tests of proposed representation and physics maps; algebraic outputs, interpretation, and open hypotheses remain separate.

nodes.title: Declared Cayley-Dickson multiplication convention
nodes.summary: The recursive product and basis/sign convention implemented by cd_core.py and the adjacent legacy kernels; a result under this convention is not automatically convention independent.

nodes.title: Sedenion assessor, null-space, and orbit structure
nodes.summary: The finite basis-element structures historically compressed as '42 ZD pairs' are separated into 42 unordered assessor axis-planes, 84 signed vectors e_a +/- e_b for a<b, 168 index-ordered representations, and explicitly conventioned annihilating-pair counts; the assessors form seven six-element classes.

nodes.title: Projected versus ambient algebraic symmetry
nodes.summary: A Lie algebra that closes in the ambient algebra need not remain closed after restriction to a selected null space; rank, closure, nondegeneracy, and basis invariance must be checked after projection.

nodes.title: Hypercomplex workbench evidence boundary
nodes.summary: The graph records finite algebraic and numerical outputs without converting them into Standard Model, particle, observable, or TOE claims.
includes: declared Cayley-Dickson convention and finite arrays
sedenion assessor, null-space, orbit, and multiplication diagnostics
finite associator and higher-algebra identity checks
projected closure, rank, Casimir, and portability diagnostics
local toy-potential minima and mechanism controls
excludes: a proof for every Cayley-Dickson convention or dimension
identification of assessors with physical Higgs particles
a measured mass, mixing angle, coupling, or new-particle prediction
external peer ratification or external KG promotion

nodes.title: The finite sedenion assessor and orbit chain is reproduced
nodes.statement: Under the declared sedenion multiplication convention, the direct calculation records 42 unordered assessor axis-planes organized into seven six-element classes, 84 signed primitive vectors e_a +/- e_b with a<b, and 168 representations when both index orders are counted.
nodes.summary: Supported as a finite combinatorial statement. These are distinct counted objects, not three synonyms. The historical labels '42 ZD pairs' and 'Higgs candidates' are not inherited; annihilating-pair totals require an explicit sign and ordering convention.

nodes.title: The recorded XOR label reproduces the seven assessor classes
nodes.statement: For the frozen finite multiplication table, all 105 tested multiplication relations match the XOR label and the 42 assessor records take one of seven class labels.
nodes.summary: Supported within the finite basis convention; no particle quantum number follows from the label.

nodes.title: The recorded finite higher-algebra identities pass
nodes.statement: The frozen S3 and S5 result arrays record the tested Jacobiator-associator, Stasheff, Hochschild-cocycle, and BV residual identities within their declared finite cases.
nodes.summary: Supported as finite exact or numerical checks, not as a general theorem over all elements or a physical interaction model.

nodes.title: The frozen projected triples realize custodial SU(2) x SU(2)
nodes.statement: For each of the 42 frozen null-space candidates, the selected projected left and right triples separately close and span independent rank-three factors whose combined rank is six.
nodes.summary: Contradicted: 42 of 42 fail both declared closure conditions, and the portability audit measures combined rank three rather than six.

nodes.title: Queue 03 supplies a basis-portable threshold verdict
nodes.statement: The legacy entrywise maximum of the projected cross-commutator is invariant under an orthogonal change of null-space basis, so its threshold crossings define a portable scientific verdict.
nodes.summary: Contradicted by the adversarial rotation audit. The legacy output is retained as history but classified NONPORTABLE_FAIL with no new physics verdict.

nodes.title: The frozen toy vacuum scans contain the recorded local minima
nodes.statement: Within the explicit Queue-04 and Queue-05 toy potentials, the stored optimizer outputs contain the declared theta-near-pi and bounded symmetry-breaking minima for the enumerated cases.
nodes.summary: Supported only for the implemented toy potentials; it is not a Standard Model vacuum or an external physical prediction.

nodes.title: Inter-orbit gamma repulsion causes the recorded single-orbit selection
nodes.statement: The repaired Queue-06 single-orbit result requires nonzero cooperative gamma coupling and is not already selected by the asymmetric alpha depths.
nodes.summary: Contradicted: the committed repair finds gamma_critical=0; the alpha perturbation already selects orbit one.

nodes.title: The repaired toy selects one orbit through the alpha perturbation
nodes.statement: Within the repaired finite Queue-06 toy, the alpha-depth asymmetry alone produces the stored single-active-orbit minimum at gamma equal to zero.
nodes.summary: Supported locally by the repaired output; its mapped historical runner is superseded and the result is not a physical vacuum claim.

nodes.title: The original projected sedenion construction establishes the g2 representation
nodes.statement: Applying the octonion inner-derivation formula in the non-alternative sedenion ambient and projecting to the seven orbit representatives yields a closed irreducible rank-14 g2 representation.
nodes.summary: Contradicted: the diagnostic finds rank 16 and a non-scalar Casimir. The original confirmation was demoted to METHOD_ARTIFACT.

nodes.title: The automorphism-embedded sidecar recovers rank 14 and antisymmetry
nodes.statement: Within the recorded automorphism-embedded sidecar, the generated action has rank 14 and passes the declared antisymmetry check.
nodes.summary: Supported only for the recorded sidecar construction; this does not imply full Lie-closure, scalar Casimir, a sedenion-ambient g2 theorem, or a physics embedding.

nodes.title: The automorphism-embedded sidecar fully validates the repaired g2 action
nodes.statement: The later 15-dimensional automorphism-embedded sidecar supplies rank, antisymmetry, Lie-closure, and Casimir controls sufficient to validate the full repaired representation.
nodes.summary: Contradicted by the recorded full controls: despite rank 14 and antisymmetry, the sidecar reports a D3 Lie-closure residual near one and D4 Casimir spread one. Producer provenance remains a separate open issue.

nodes.title: The explicit sigma and Psi maps generate an S3 automorphism subgroup
nodes.statement: Under the declared multiplication convention, sigma and Psi preserve all 256 tested basis products, have presentation orders 2, 3, and 2, and generate a six-element group with order fingerprint one identity, three involutions, and two order-three elements.
nodes.summary: Supported as the explicit finite three-gate calculation. It does not by itself prove a direct-product decomposition, a three-generation model, or a physical symmetry.

nodes.title: The Queue-09 multiplication test refutes Wilmot 2025
nodes.statement: Because the two explicit maps pass multiplication preservation, Wilmot 2025 claimed that no S3 automorphism exists and is therefore refuted.
nodes.summary: Contradicted by the 2026-07-12 source correction: Wilmot does not make the attributed G2-only claim, and the Brown/Wilmot distinction is reframed as strong versus weak automorphism criteria.

nodes.title: The finite algebraic regularities establish Standard Model referents
nodes.statement: The currently indexed hypercomplex subset jointly determines physical Higgs fields, gauge groups, three generations, measured constants, or new particles from its assessor counts, orbit labels, higher-algebra identities, and automorphism checks.
nodes.summary: Not established in the indexed subset. No validated referent map is present and several specific projected routes are contradicted, while the finite algebraic facts remain useful. Partial coverage is not a universal no-go theorem, so an external discriminator remains open.

nodes.title: Finite sedenion structure and higher-algebra result ledger
nodes.summary: The committed results record the assessor list, seven six-element classes, 105-of-105 XOR agreement, and the declared finite S3/S5 identity residuals. The direct Avenue-3 scripts separate 42 assessor planes, 84 signed vectors with a<b, and 168 index-ordered representations; they also report 168 unordered any-sign annihilating unit-pairs and 336 ordered products, while the all-plus count changes from 84 ordered to 42 after unordered canonicalization. Bare 'pair' language is therefore withheld.

nodes.title: The recorded Claim B nullity distribution stabilizes from n=5 to n=7
nodes.statement: Under the sealed-loop predicate, the simple-zero-divisor nullity distributions at n=5,6,7 approach one another with total-variation distances below 0.05 and a decreasing n=6 to n=7 distance.
nodes.summary: Contradicted by the committed result: TV(5,6)=0.476190 and TV(6,7)=0.488189, both far above 0.05, with the latter slightly larger.

nodes.title: The recorded Claim B associator distribution stabilizes from n=4 to n=7
nodes.statement: Under the sealed-loop predicate, consecutive seed-42 associator-ratio distributions cease to reconfigure, with no two consecutive Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics above 0.05.
nodes.summary: Contradicted: the recorded consecutive KS statistics are 0.1484, 0.1072, and 0.1036, so the registered reconfiguration condition is met repeatedly even though the mean changes become smaller.

nodes.title: The recorded Claim B prediction family is Cauchy-decreasing from n=5 to n=7
nodes.statement: For every stored component of P_n=(mean associator ratio, modal nullity, zero-divisor density), the n=6 to n=7 change is strictly smaller than the n=5 to n=6 change and passes the registered guards.
nodes.summary: Contradicted by the stored predicate result, which records cauchy_ok=false and a zero-denominator guard for modal nullity. The finite result is labelled DRIFTING rather than a theorem about n to infinity.

nodes.title: The finite Claim B loop establishes or universally rules out infinite-tower gravity
nodes.statement: The n=4 through n=7 statistical loop alone defines the infinite Cayley-Dickson limit, its path-integral measure and action, and a gravity observable map, or else proves that no such construction can exist.
nodes.summary: Not established. The loop kills its registered finite statistical stability route and retains the algebra-to-observable barrier; it neither constructs the infinite object nor supplies a universal no-go over other completions and measures.

nodes.title: The explicit S3 action centralizes the computed derivation space
nodes.statement: In the recorded finite matrix audit, the sedenion derivation equations have a 14-dimensional numerical null space and conjugation by both explicit S3 generators acts as the identity on that computed space within 8.9e-16 infinity norm.
nodes.summary: Supported as a finite numerical action statement with positive and fake-map controls. It supports a direct action on the computed derivation factor, not a classification of the full automorphism group.

nodes.title: The explicit S3 maps preserve the recorded Wilmot eq-9 theta tensor
nodes.statement: For both stored Cayley-Dickson sign conventions, the independently transcribed Wilmot eq-9 theta support aligns exactly up to the recorded global sign with the alternating structure constants, and sigma and Psi preserve it with residuals 0 and 2.78e-17.
nodes.summary: Supported for the two implemented conventions and one transcribed tensor. This corrects the old same-convention 'Wilmot refuted' story and leaves the cross-primary realization open.

nodes.title: The finite direct-action test proves the full automorphism-group decomposition
nodes.statement: The computed 14-dimensional derivation space and trivial conjugation action of the explicit S3 generators are sufficient by themselves to prove that every sedenion automorphism lies in a globally classified direct product Aut(S)=G2 x S3.
nodes.summary: Not established by the finite audit. The calculation identifies an explicit subgroup action and centralization of a computed infinitesimal space, but does not prove completeness, connected-component integration, absence of other automorphisms, or cross-primary equivalence.
